sentences.text:
Smt.Narayanamma and Sri. Muniswamy asserting to be injured, suffered in a road traffic accident,
filed petitions under Sec.166 of I.M.V.Act, claiming compensation from the respondents who are the insured and owner of the Tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 alleging that on 25.09.2019 at 6.30 p.m., when Muniswamy was riding Moped bearing No.KA-49-I-136 by keeping Smt.Narayanamma on the pillion on Bethamangala-Kyasamballi road, near Subramanya temple, Byatarayanahalli village, KGF Taluk, driver of a Tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 drove the same negligently suddenly applied the brake of the tractor on the middle of the road, made the moped to dash to the rear part of the tractor, thereby became the reason for the accident, resulting in injuries to the petitioners.

Regarding the accident, Bethamangala police registered a case in Cr.No.125/2019.
c/w 3298/2020 2.

Petitioners took treatment at Bethamangala Community Hospital and Bowring Hospital,
Bengaluru.
As on the date of accident, Smt. Narayanamma being aged about 68 years, Muniswamy being aged about 71 years, used to earn Rs.15,000/- and Rs.20,000/- per month respectively by doing agriculture.

3. In response to the notice, the respondents No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective Advocates and filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioners.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 23.03.2021 this Authority has framed the following issues:-
MVC No.3295/2020 1)Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a Motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.09.2019 at about 6.30 p.m., near Subramanya temple,
Byatarayanahalli village, Bethamangala-Kyasamballi road, KGF, within the jurisdiction of Bethamangala police station on account of rah and negligent driving of the Tractor bearing registration No.AP-03-CD-3414 by its driver when the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider in the TVS XL bearing reg.No.KA-40-I-136 ?
c/w 3298/2020 2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, how much and from whom ?
3) What order ?

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 25.09.2019 at about 6.30 p.m., near Subramanya temple, Byatarayanahalli village,
Bethamangala-Kyasamballi road, KGF, within the jurisdiction of Bethamangala police station on account of rah and negligent driving of the Tractor bearing registration No.AP-03-CD-3414 by its Muniswamy vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50997998/
2 driver when the petitioner was riding the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA-40-I-136 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, how much and from whom ?
3. What order ?
5. On 04.11.2023, 09.06.2023, Smt.Narayanamma deposed as PW.1 and produced 9 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.9.
On 10.03.2023 and 09.06.2023 Muniswamy deposed as PW.2 and produced 4 documents at Exs.P.10 to P.13.

On 20.09.2023, petitioner produced evidence of Medical Record c/w 3298/2020 Keeper of Bowring Hospital as PW.3 and get produced 8 documents at Exs.P.14 to P.21.
6.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of the petitioners, respondent No.1.

In these cases,
respondent No.2/owner of the Tractor does not come forward to submit arguments.
I have perused the entire records 7.

On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
MVC No.3295/2020 Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.25,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
MVC No.3298/2020 Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.96,810/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issue No.1 in both the cases :- In the evidence PW.1 & 2 Smt.Narayanamma and Muniswamy stated that on c/w 3298/2020 25.09.2019 at 6.30 p.m., when Muniswamy riding a moped bearing No.kA-40-I-136 by keeping Smt.Narayanamma on the pillion on Bethamangala-Kyasamballi road,
near Subramanya temple, Byatarayanahalli Village, KGF Taluk, driver of a tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 drove the same negligently, applied the brake on the middle of the road, thereby made the moped to dash to the rear part of the tractor resulting in injuries to the petitioners.
In the written statement, the respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

9. In the cross-examination, PW.1 Smt.Narayanamma stated that the place of accident is a small road and denied the suggestion that there was no fault on the part of the driver of the tractor to the accident and due to the negligence of her husband, the accident taken place.

In the cross-examination, PW.2 Muniswamy stated that the place of accident is a small road and denied the suggestion that there was no fault on the part of the driver of the tractor and due to his negligence, the accident was taken place.
PW.2 denied the suggestion that he dashed the moped to the rear part of the tractor by negligently driving c/w 3298/2020 the moped.
PW.2 stated that as the tractor driver suddenly applied the brake, the moped came in contact to the rear part of the tractor.
11. In the evidence PW.3/Medical record keeper of Bowring Hospital produced copy of the MLC register, copy of the police intimation, case sheet, discharge summary, X-ray at Exs.P.15 to P.21.
In the cross-examination PW.3 stated that the doctors wrote the contents in MLC register.

12. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Cr.No.125/2019 of Bethamangala police station, registered on 27.09.2019 against the driver of the tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC, regarding collision taken place between the rear part of the tractor and front part of the moped bearing No.KA-40-I-136 at 6.30 p.m., on 25.09.2019, on the basis of the complaint presented by PW.1 Smt.Narayanamma w/o Muniswamy/ PW.1.
Ex . P.2
is the spot mahazar recorded on 28.09.2019 (in the back page, date of recording of mahazar is noted as 28.09.2010).
Ex . P.3
is the copy of the sketch recorded on 28.09.2019.
Exs . P.4
and P.5

are the copy of the notice c/w 3298/2020 issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act, by the Investigation Officer to the respondent No.2/owner of the tractor and reply dated 02.10.2019 issued by the respondent No.2 to the Investigation Officer.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the motor vehicle accident report dated 01.10.2019.
Ex.P.7 & P.10 are the copy of wound certificates pertaining to Smt.Narayanamma and Muniswamy.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Bethamangala police against Ambareesh-driver of the tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

In the medical records, the reason for the injuries suffered by Narayanamma and Muniswamy are noted as 'alleged history of RTA while riding two wheeler on 25.09.2019 at 6.30 p.m., near Byataranahalli, Kolar'.
In these cases there are no evidence/reasons to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by PW 1 and 2 regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 25.09.2019 at 6.30 p.m., when Muniswamy riding moped bearing No.KA-40-I-136 on Bethamangala-Kyasambanahalli road near Subramanya temple, Byatarayanahalli village, Ambareesh-driver of the c/w 3298/2020 tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 negligently applied the brake on the middle of the road, thereby made the moped to dash to the rear part of the tractor, resulting in the injuries to Smt.Narayanamma and Muniswamy-riders of the moped.
Hence, I have answered Issue No.1 in both the cases in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2 in MVC No.3295/2020 :

In the evidence PW.1 Smt.Narayanamma stated that in the accident, she has suffered injuries, took treatment at Community Hospital, Bethamangala, SNR Hospital, Kolar, by spending Rs.3 Lakhs and as on the date of accident, used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month by doing agriculture.
In the written statement, the respondents denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by Smt.Narayanamma.
In the cross-examination, PW.1 denied the suggestion that as per wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, she has suffered only simple injuries.

sentences.text: Wound Certificate, case sheet and medical records shows that in the accident Smt.Narayanamma suffered lacerated wound on right scalp, took treatment at Community Hospital, Bethamangala.
In the wound c/w 3298/2020 certificate nature of the injuries suffered by Smt.Narayanamma is noted as 'simple'.
Hence, Rs.25,000/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum is awarded to Smt.Narayanamma.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 in MVC No.3295/2020 accordingly.
15. Issue No.2 in MVC No.3298/2020 :

In the evidence PW.2 Muniswamy stated that in the accident, he has suffered injuries all over the body, took treatment at Bethamangala Community Hospital, then took treatment at Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru, by spending Rs.3 lakhs and as on the date of accident, used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by doing agriculture.
In the cross-examination PW.2 denied the suggestion that in the accident he has suffered only simple injuries.

16. Wound Certificate, case sheet, x-ray, medical bills shows that in the accident PW.2-Muniswamy suffered frontal haemorrhage with frail chest with TCP insertion insitu with spleenic injury, took treatment at Community Health Center, Bethamangala, then took treatment at Bowring Hospital,
Bengaluru, as an inpatient from 26.09.2019 to 09.10.2019 by spending Rs.3,810/-.

In this c/w 3298/2020 case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by PW.2 Muniswamy regarding nature of injury, length, place and nature of treatment taken for those injuries.

Hence, Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering,
Rs.3,810/- is awarded towards treatment charges, Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards attendant and conveyance charges and Rs.28,000/- ( Rs.14,000 x 2) is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner in MVC No.3298/2020 is entitle to receive Rs.96,810/-
with current and future interest at 6% per annum as compensation.
17. In the written statement the respondent No.1/insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show contravention of any terms of the policy by the respondent No.2 as on the date of accident.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that in both the cases respondents being c/w 3298/2020 the insurer and owner of the tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD- 3414 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
Petitions
filed under Sec.166 of IMV Act are partly allowed in the following terms:

In MVC No.3295/2020 the respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the petitioner-Smt.Narayanamma towards compensation.

In MVC No.3298/2020 the respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.96,810/- (Rupees Ninety Six Thousand Eight Hundred and Ten) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the petitioner- Muniswamy vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50997998/
5 Muniswamy towards compensation.
In both the cases, respondent No.1 being the insurer of tractor bearing No.AP-03-CD-3414 shall deposit compensation amount and interest within three months from today.
After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their bank account directly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- each.
Draw an Award accordingly.

Office is directed to keep the original of this Judgment in MVC No.3295/2020 and a copy thereof in MVC No.3298/2020.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 14 th day of August, 2024.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
